hook_text: For twenty-seven years, he was the most famous prisoner in the world. Then, one Sunday afternoon, he walked out into the sun.
clip_script: 2 February 1990. Parliament, Cape Town. President F.W. de Klerk stands up and says the words nobody expected: the ANC, the PAC and the Communist Party are no longer banned. And Nelson Mandela will be released. Nine days later, on Sunday 11 February, crowds gather outside Victor Verster Prison near Paarl. Cameras from all over the world are waiting. Mandela walks out of the gate, holding Winnie's hand, and raises his fist. That evening, from the balcony of Cape Town City Hall, he speaks: not as a prophet, but as a humble servant of the people. Exiles start coming home to families they have not seen for years. Apartheid laws begin to fall. But nobody can vote yet. The hardest part has only just begun.
visual_style: Parliament in session; a newspaper headline; crowds lining a road; a prison gate opening; a raised fist; the City Hall balcony and the Grand Parade packed with people; families hugging at an airport.
mood: Joyful and historic, with a hint of uncertainty.
pacing: Building anticipation, then a celebratory peak, then a thoughtful close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand the unbanning of political movements and the release of Mandela in 1990.
